name: Royal Caribbean Group
description: Royal Caribbean Group is the world's second-largest cruise operator by revenue, operating a multi-brand portfolio spanning mass-market/contemporary (Royal Caribbean International), premium (Celebrity Cruises) and ultra-luxury/expedition (Silversea) tiers, plus a 50%-owned joint venture in TUI Cruises/Hapag-Lloyd Cruises. Revenue is earned in two forms: passenger ticket revenue (the upfront cabin fare, booked well in advance) and onboard and other revenue (spending once aboard — dining, beverages, casino, shore excursions, and increasingly the company's private island destinations such as Perfect Day at CocoCay). The company reports as a single operating and reportable segment; brand-level financials are not separately disclosed. Profitability is driven by net yield (revenue per available berth day) growth, high occupancy (often above 100% given double/triple cabin occupancy), and disciplined cost control (net cruise costs excluding fuel), financed by a long-dated newbuild pipeline of larger, more efficient ships.

employees.note: ~11,450 shoreside (4,450 U.S., 5,450 international, ~1,600 at private destinations) and ~96,500 shipboard, of which 87% are covered by collective bargaining agreements

businessLines.name: Passenger ticket revenue
businessLines.description: Upfront cabin fare paid by guests, booked in advance across all brands; RCL does not disclose this split by brand.
businessLines.revenueNote: Approximately 70% of total FY2025 revenues of $17,935M; exact dollar figure not independently confirmed in sources reviewed

businessLines.name: Onboard and other revenue
businessLines.description: Spending once aboard — food and beverage, casino, shore excursions, WiFi/connectivity, and revenue from RCL's private destinations (Perfect Day at CocoCay and other island stops).
businessLines.revenueNote: Approximately 30% of total FY2025 revenues of $17,935M; exact dollar figure not independently confirmed in sources reviewed
